deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is writing up the theory of singular values ρ_i(u) of compact operators between Hilbert spaces, as preparation for the next section, 'Classes remarquables d'opérateurs dans l'espace de Hilbert', which treats Schatten's theory in a form simplified by Weyl-type inequalities. Throughout, ρ_1(u) ≥ ρ_2(u) ≥ ... are the singular values of u (the eigenvalues of |u| = (u*u)^{1/2}, in decreasing order).

Th. 4 (titled 'théorème K. de convexité dans les espaces de Hilbert').
- Hypotheses: E, F are Hilbert spaces; u, v: E → F are compact. φ(s_1, ..., s_n) is a convex, symmetric function on s_i ≥ 0 that is increasing in each argument. The struck-out first version assumed instead that f(e^{t_1}, ..., e^{t_n}) is convex, which is the multiplicative hypothesis of Corollary 4 on the previous page.
- Conclusion (41): φ(ρ_1(u+v), ..., ρ_n(u+v)) ≤ φ(ρ_1(u)+ρ_1(v), ..., ρ_n(u)+ρ_n(v)).
- Proof: by 'Th. 1, 1°' together with the convexity lemma of 'No 1'. Th. 1, 1° is presumably Ky Fan's maximum principle, Σ_{i≤k} ρ_i(u) = max |Σ_{i≤k} (u e_i, f_i)| over orthonormal systems. It gives the additive weak majorization Σ_{i≤k} ρ_i(u+v) ≤ Σ_{i≤k} (ρ_i(u)+ρ_i(v)) for all k. The lemma of No 1 is presumably the Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya / Karamata / Tomić–Weyl lemma: weak majorization implies φ(x) ≤ φ(y) for every symmetric convex increasing φ.
- A struck-out corollary (42) is the special case φ(s) = Σ g(s_i) with g convex increasing (and g(0) = 0).

Corollary 1.
- Let N be a 'Schatten norm' on R^n, that is, a symmetric gauge function in von Neumann's sense: symmetric, depending only on |x_i|, increasing on the positive orthant, normalized; this is Définition 1 on the next page.
- Set ||u||_N = N(ρ_1(u), ..., ρ_n(u)) (43). Then the triangle inequality (44) holds: ||u+v||_N ≤ ||u||_N + ||v||_N.
- Proof: N restricted to s_i ≥ 0 satisfies the hypotheses of (41). Then N(ρ(u)+ρ(v)) ≤ N(ρ(u)) + N(ρ(v)) because N is a norm.

Corollary 2.
- For u, v in L^p_0(E, F), the Schatten p-class (1 ≤ p ≤ ∞), apply Corollary 1 to N_p and let n → ∞. This gives (45) (Σ ρ_i(u+v)^p)^{1/p} ≤ (Σ ρ_i(u)^p)^{1/p} + (Σ ρ_i(v)^p)^{1/p}.
- Hence (46) ||u+v||_p ≤ ||u||_p + ||v||_p: the Schatten p-'norms' really are norms.

Purpose: establish that the symmetric norm ideals / Schatten classes are normed spaces. This is the additive counterpart of the multiplicative (Horn/Weyl-type) Hölder inequalities (35)–(40) on the previous page.
errors: No substantive error. (41) holds exactly under the stated hypotheses, since the Ky Fan weak majorization plus the Tomić–Weyl/HLP lemma suffices for convex, symmetric, increasing φ.
Minor gap: Corollary 2 for infinite sums and for p = ∞ needs an explicit passage to the limit n → ∞ (and sup for p = ∞); this is only implicit in the text.
The proof of Th. 4 is only sketched by reference to 'Th. 1, 1°' and 'No 1', which are not on this page.

ideas.what: For compact u, v and any symmetric convex increasing φ: φ(ρ(u+v)) ≤ φ(ρ(u)+ρ(v)), via weak majorization of singular values
ideas.modern_name: Ky Fan's singular value inequality for sums (weak majorization) combined with the Tomić–Weyl / Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya convexity lemma
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ky Fan (1951, PNAS); Tomić (1949), H. Weyl (1949); Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya (1929/1934)
ideas.where_published: Not, to my knowledge, in his 1955 Memoir 'Produits tensoriels topologiques' in this form; possibly in the São Paulo course notes on topological vector spaces – unsure

ideas.what: Triangle inequality for unitarily invariant norms ||u||_N = N(ρ(u)) defined by a symmetric gauge function N
ideas.modern_name: Unitarily invariant norms / symmetric norming functions, symmetrically normed ideals
ideas.usually_credited_to: von Neumann (1937), Schatten (1946/1950), Ky Fan (1951); later Gohberg–Krein

ideas.what: Schatten p-classes are normed (Minkowski inequality for singular values)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schatten–von Neumann (1946–48), Schatten 'A theory of cross-spaces' (1950)
ideas.where_published: Related material in 'Produits tensoriels topologiques' (1955), ch. II

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean expository derivation of standard results: Ky Fan dominance, the convexity lemma, and the triangle inequality for Schatten / unitarily invariant norms. All were known by 1951. The only point of interest is Grothendieck's choice of a 'simplified' route through Weyl/Ky Fan majorization, which is itself the standard modern route.
